description: Switch to manual uninstall/install updates and add editable login account management

Added Edit User capability in the login window for user name/profile updates and password changes

description: Add launch-learning controls, Program Builder, and secure secret vault management
notes: Added a learning system that tracks launch flow history, recommends startup order, supports optional auto-apply, and supports per-run user override
Added a Program Builder tab for creating/updating launch steps directly in-app, including program paths, login sequences, timing, and productivity notes
Added secure secret handling with encrypted local storage and runtime token resolution using {{secret:Name}}
Added full secret management in-app: save, list, rename, delete, and token insertion for login sequences

description: Fix early SQL login timeout and restore visible install progress on self-update
notes: The SQL Server login/password wait was counting loop iterations as whole seconds, but iterations that dismissed an Access confirmation dialog only took 400-1000ms, so the configured timeout could be exhausted in far less real time than intended right before the real login box appeared
The wait now tracks real elapsed time with a stopwatch instead of iteration count, and won't repeatedly re-process the same confirmation dialog it already tried to dismiss
Self-update installs now run the installer non-silently so its own wizard can ask to confirm, show real install progress, and offer to relaunch Launcher when the update finishes

description: Fix update table flow stuck on Access confirmation dialog; show install progress
notes: Access shows an intermediate 'You are about to update N record(s)' confirmation dialog before the real SQL Server login box, which has no password field and needs a Yes/OK click
The update table flow now recognizes a detected window without an edit field as this confirmation, dismisses it automatically, and keeps waiting for the real login prompt before typing the password
Added a small delay between simulated mouse-down and mouse-up in the button-click fallback for extra reliability

After downloading an update, the app now shows an 'Installing update...' message instead of closing silently, and the installer auto-relaunches Launcher when a silent self-update finishes so the app reappearing signals completion

description: Fix password sometimes going into a transient message box instead of the SQL Server login box
notes: Access can briefly flash a transient message box (e.g. a security/loading notice) before the real SQL Server login box appears
The password-window detection previously grabbed the first new window it saw, which could be that transient box; if it closed on its own before the password was typed, the real login box was missed
Detection now re-checks a candidate window after a short settle delay and keeps waiting if it already closed, instead of typing into a window that's gone

description: Fix password sometimes entered before the SQL Server login box appears
notes: 'Microsoft Access' was configured as a password-window title to match, but that title also belongs to Access's own background frame window, which is already open before the Update Table button is clicked
The password-window detection now requires every candidate match to be a genuinely new window since the button click, not just the fallback path, closing the false-positive gap
'Microsoft Access' was moved out of the match list and into the exclude list in launcher.config.json

description: Give the update-table step more time to finish
notes: Increased the update-table flow's post-password wait from 180 to 240 seconds
Ensures the Visual Board table update has finished before the launcher proceeds to the next step

description: Fix installer hanging during silent installs/updates
notes: The installer's "already installed, remove first?" and "launch now?" prompts used MessageBox, which NSIS does not auto-dismiss during silent (/S) installs, so a silent install could hang forever waiting for a click
The installer now detects silent mode and skips those prompts entirely (auto-removing the previous version, and not auto-launching), so /S installs always complete on their own
This directly affects the app's own self-update flow, which installs updates with /S

description: Split About and Check for Updates into separate windows
notes: Help > About and Help > Check for Updates now open two completely separate windows instead of sharing one tabbed window
Clicking About only shows the about info; clicking Check for Updates only shows update checking/download
Reordered the Help menu so Check for Updates is listed first and About is last

description: Make the Stop button clearly visible even when disabled
notes: Confirmed via UI Automation that the Stop button was always present and correctly positioned in the running app
The button's disabled appearance previously fell back to the OS default theme, which washed its custom red coloring out to a near-invisible gray against the app's dark background
The Stop button now uses its own custom styling at all times: a clearly muted dark red when idle/disabled, and a bright red when a run is active and it can be clicked

description: Move Check for Updates to its own Help menu item
notes: Check for Updates is now its own item in the Help menu (alongside About), instead of only being reachable as a tab inside the About window
Clicking Help > Check for Updates opens directly to the Updates tab and immediately starts checking
The Stop button (added in 1.1.30) remains available on the main window whenever a Start/Close run is in progress

description: Add a dedicated Updates tab with real download progress; close automatically instead of asking
notes: Added a dedicated Updates tab to the About window, separate from the general About info
Download & Install now shows a real in-app progress bar (percentage and MB downloaded/total) instead of an external PowerShell console window
Removed the confirmation dialog that asked to close Launcher before installing; it now closes automatically once the download is verified and the installer is launched
Update checking, downloading, and checksum verification now run in-process via a new LauncherUpdateService

description: Fix update table sending password before SQL Server login box appears; add Stop button
notes: Generic fallback titles like Access/Microsoft Access matched the main Access window instantly, so the update table flow assumed the SQL Server password prompt was up and typed into whatever had focus

The update table flow now genuinely watches for the SQL Server login/password window (specific configured titles, then any window newly appeared since the Update Table button was clicked) before typing the password
Added a Stop button to the Launcher UI to halt a running Start/Close automation immediately
Rebuilt the installer for these fixes

description: Fix login-success detection falsely declaring Visual Board login complete
notes: The Enter-retry logic in the native login flow treated the main Access window being visible as proof of login success, but that window title is present the entire time Access is running, even during the login form
This let the flow declare login done after the very first attempt, skipping retries and the failure check, leaving the app stuck on the login form while later steps proceeded anyway
Login success is now judged solely by the login window itself closing, matching the legacy PowerShell contract
Rebuilt the installer for the login-success-detection fix

description: Fix update table flow racing ahead of Visual Board login
notes: The main Access window title appears immediately on launch, even while the login form is still processing, so the old window-title-only check let update table clicks start too early

The update table flow now waits for the real post-login control (the Update Table button, or a configured loginReadyControlNames list) to actually appear before clicking, matching the legacy PowerShell behavior
Added a configurable loginReadyTimeoutSeconds (default 60s) for this wait
Rebuilt the installer for the login-readiness fix

description: Restore 1.1.0 Visual Board login behavior in native start flow
notes: Direct UI-Automation value injection is now only used when a step explicitly configures loginFieldValue, matching the legacy PowerShell contract
Visual Board now always types the full login sequence with real keystrokes instead of a synthetic value write that Access did not reliably register
Added a real mouse click on the login field before focusing it, matching the legacy click-then-focus behavior
Rebuilt the installer for the login-behavior regression fix

description: Fix Visual Board login targeting regression in native start flow

Rebuilt the installer for the 1.1.26 release line
